topic.title: Introduction
topic.description: Overview of math, characters, and strings

sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s explore the building blocks of Java programming! Today, we’ll cover:

• How computers handle numbers and math
• The difference between characters and strings
• Why these concepts matter in real code

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you’re building a digital recipe app. Math helps calculate ingredient quantities, while characters and strings let users type their favorite recipes.

**Numbers in Java**
• Java has different number types (like `int` for whole numbers, `double` for decimals)
• Example: `int eggs = 12;` stores how many eggs you have

**Characters vs Strings**
• A *character* is a single letter/symbol (`'A'`, `'$'`, `'7'`) 
• A *string* is a sequence of characters (`"Hello!"`, `"12 eggs"`)

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Strings can mix with numbers (but watch your `+` signs!)

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use `double` for money to avoid rounding errors
Add spaces in strings for readability: `"Hello " + name`
donts: Don’t start variable names with numbers (`1var` is invalid)
Don’t forget semicolons at the end of statements!
sections.protip: Use `final` for constants (e.g., `final double PI = 3.14`) to prevent accidental changes

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where you’ll see this in action:

examples.how: Calculates interest with `double` and formats receipts with strings
Counts characters in posts (`char`) and displays usernames (`String`)

problem.description:
Write a program that:
1. Stores your age as an `int`
2. Stores your first initial as a `char`
3. Prints a message like "J is 25 years old!"
hints: Remember: `char` uses single quotes, `String` uses double quotes
Combine them with `+` (e.g., initial + " is " + age)
problem.explanation: We used `int` for age (whole number) and `char` for the initial. The `+` operator combines them into one string for printing.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Practice mixing math and strings for dynamic output
📌 Ready to learn loops next – they’ll make this 10x more powerful!
